Epic Games will abandon blueprints right at the launch of Unreal Engine 6
Published by
admin
Tags:
Epic Games
,
Unreal Engine 6
Epic Games has revised its plans for the upcoming Unreal Engine 6. The company
announced
that it will not support blueprints and the Actor Gameplay Framework even in the early versions of the engine. These will be replaced by the Scene Graph gameplay system, built on the Verse programming language.
Fortnite
Notably, back in June, Epic Games expressed a desire to keep these tools at least at the launch of Unreal Engine 6. It was expected that this would allow developers to transition projects from Unreal Engine 5 to the updated engine without undue haste. However, almost six months later, the company reconsidered and decided to expedite the transition to the new architecture utilizing artificial intelligence capabilities.
According to Epic Games, it changed its stance after recent tests with Fortnite.
“Fortnite has one of the largest libraries of Blueprints anywhere. Two weeks ago, we experimented with using AI to convert all of the Blueprints for Battle Royale to Verse. This project was expected to take years, but we now have a working prototype of Fortnite that is about 3 million lines of Verse code after porting more than 20,000 Blueprints. The team is hard at work iterating to validate the resulting performance, memory usage, and architecture. We’re doing this at scale now, and this conversion will help make the process as easy as possible for everyone else,” explained Epic Games Vice President Marcus Wassmer (Marcus Wassmer).
The announcement from Epic Games caused a negative reaction within the game development community. Specifically, the phasing out of blueprints and the Actor Gameplay Framework was criticized by former Valve writer Chet Faliszek, who stated that the company is depriving developers of convenient tools that allowed for the creation of game mechanics without in-depth programming knowledge. Developers will now either have to learn Verse or rely on AI.
It should be noted that back in October, Epic Games announced the company’s focus on AI. It believes that neural networks will accelerate workflows and enable more things to be achieved with fewer resources.
